title: LION: A Clifford Neural Paradigm for Multimodal-Attributed Graph Learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.24795v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recently, the rapid advancement of multimodal domains has driven a data-centric paradigm shift in graph ML, transitioning from text-attributed to multimodal-attributed graphs. This advancement significantly enhances data representation and expands the scope of graph downstream tasks, such as modality-oriented tasks, thereby improving the practical utility of graph ML. Despite its promise, limitations exist in the current neural paradigms:(1) Neglect Context in Modality Alignment: Most existing methods adopt topology-constrained or modality-specific operators as tokenizers.These aligners inevitably neglect graph context and inhibit modality interaction, resulting in suboptimal alignment.(2) Lack of Adaptation in Modality Fusion: Most existing methods are simple adaptations for 2-modality graphs and fail to adequately exploit aligned tokens equipped with topology priors during fusion, leading to poor generalizability and performance degrad

translated_title: LION：一种用于多模态属性图学习的克利福德神经范式
translated_abstract: 摘要：近期，多模态领域的快速发展推动了图机器学习中数据中心的范式转变，从文本属性图转向多模态属性图。这一进展显著增强了数据表示能力，并扩展了图下游任务的范围，例如面向模态的任务，从而提高了图机器学习的实际应用价值。尽管前景广阔，当前神经范式仍存在局限性：（1）模态对齐中忽略上下文：大多数现有方法采用拓扑约束或模态特定算子作为分词器，这些对齐器不可避免地忽略图上下文并抑制模态交互，导致对齐效果欠佳。（2）模态融合中缺乏适应性：大多数现有方法是对双模态图的简单适配，未能在融合过程中充分利用带有拓扑先验的对齐令牌，导致泛化能力差和性能下降。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于克利福德代数的神经范式LION，通过上下文感知的模态对齐和拓扑先验的模态融合，解决了多模态属性图学习中现有方法忽略上下文和缺乏适应性的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes LION, a Clifford neural paradigm that addresses context neglect in modality alignment and lack of adaptation in modality fusion for multimodal-attributed graph learning.
